stimulus.text:
The Selective Service Act, approved May 18, 1917, Section 5 (verbatim excerpts):

"That all male persons between the ages of twenty-one and thirty, both inclusive, shall be subject to registration in accordance with regulations to be prescribed by the President . . . it shall be the duty of all persons of the designated ages . . . to present themselves for and submit to registration under the provisions of this Act; and any person who shall wilfully fail or refuse to present himself for registration or to submit thereto as herein provided, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor . . ."
stimulus.source_note: Verbatim excerpts from the Selective Service Act, May 18, 1917, Section 5 (public domain).

rationales.A: With millions of men in uniform and European immigration cut off, northern factories hired Black workers from the South, and hundreds of thousands moved north.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the draft took workers from the South too, but farmland prices did not collapse because of it.
rationales.C: The Panama Canal stayed open through the war. The draft had nothing to do with it.
rationales.D: The Committee on Public Information ended after the war, not because factories needed workers.
rationales.general:
1. Follow the chain one link at a time. The draft took men out of the factories.
2. Ask who could fill those jobs. European immigration had fallen, so factories turned to Black workers in the South.
3. Name the result. Those workers moved north in the Great Migration.
Remember: a chain of causes is only as strong as its links, so check each link before you trust the end.
